doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Blues, church and the call to music
title: Communication, loneliness and his father's explanation
summary: Lloyd ties his ability to reach audiences to a lonely childhood and recounts asking his father why he did not marry his mother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes.
But I realized that early on. Even at the amateur show, I must have had a gift because I reached all them people for a standing ovation, and I wasn’t correct. I wasn’t ready to be doing that.
There was something inside that they felt.
Inside. Well, the loneliness of this little boy, you understand?
Yes, yes I do!
And the Mother leavin’ you somewhere.
Yes.

And once I asked my father, “Why did you not marry my mother?” Cause I was upset, cause he was living in Phoenix at that time. He had gone to graduate school in Tempe, and he had had his masters and doctorate and stuff. He was there - that’s strange, I graduated from that school last season and I told them to give me an honorary doctorate or somethin’, and they though I was nuts or somethin’, you know. But I had more accomplishment than many of those students...
Of course you have.

... that I went to school with. But they never, you know, they thought I was... One of the professors said “Charles Lloyd, S.C. would have been better if he had never come to school here.” You know, cause I was outspoken and stuff about all this stuff. But anyway, getting back to this thing we were talkin’ about. My father. I asked him why he didn’t marry my mother? He said, “I wanted to marry your mother.” He said, “But she
didn’t think that my prospects were good enough.”
Wow.
She married the pharmacist, the pill roller who was takin’ his own medications, and who was a dysfunctional cat! And my father was a beautiful man.
Slavery messed up the family structure so dramatically.
So that’s why. So when you asked me why I could communicate...
Yeah.
... when I saw that this uncle said, “His mother better come get him.” I said, I made a connection with the Lord at that point.
Yes.
I said, if nobody wants me, I’m gonna have to want myself, and then a light came.
Gotcha. That’s important.
And when the light came, you’re possessed with the light, and then - that’s white light that comes in - and then you have deities who are around you. Who say, well... Because many are called.
You were chosen. Wow.
I don’t know if that’s the answer to your question.
Well, it answered...
